dedupe_keys.name: indonesia rice supply chain hub locations during covid 19 with agent based modelling and robust optimisation

description: This case study designs a rice supply chain strategy that stays robust when COVID-19 reduces food production capacity. The authors, researchers at Padjadjaran University in Indonesia, published it in an open-access journal article. Because real data on uncertain production were hard to obtain during the pandemic, they used an agent-based model of upstream supply chain actors, the farmers, to simulate production capacity, and fed the resulting uncertainty set into a robust optimisation model that chooses food hub locations and the food network. Coverage is a regional rice supply chain in Indonesia. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: the agent-based model replaces missing data with simulated capacity, the case is illustrative, and the robust counterpart depends on the chosen uncertainty set. The study found that the integrated framework can handle the uncertain rice supply problem without actual uncertainty data and gives robust optimal hub locations and network flows. Simulation uses: a template for combining agent-based simulation and optimisation to plan food hubs under disruption. Related records: the staple food trade network study (case_study-global-staple-food-trade-network-resilience-cascading-failure) looks at rice supply resilience at global scale.
